Quick note from our infra team: two items to add to the parking-lot — both priority for the deep-dive:
1) Data residency + KMS integration: we need to confirm whether token KV caches contain any customer PII and whether a HSM-backed KMS flow is supported in private deployments.
2) Autoscaling behavior under bursty traffic and how request routing chooses between dedicated and hosted pools (we want to avoid cross-region fallbacks).

We can expand in the meeting but wanted these captured upfront.

Thanks Raj / team — good items. Quick clarifications from Redwood operations that will help us prepare answers:
- KV cache: by default we do not persist PII; KV caches are in-memory per serving instance and evicted on shutdown. For private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations for encryption-at-rest for any optional persistent artifacts.
- Autoscaling: routing policies are policy-driven; we can pin a route to dedicated capacity and disallow cross-region fallbacks if thats a hard constraint. Well bring details (diagram + failure modes) to the meeting.

Attaching a short datasheet with the options and our suggested defaults: [Attachment: pre-read-datasheet.md (Markdown, 8KB)]
